subject: math
title: Multiplying and Dividing Decimals
seo_title: Grade 6 Multiplying and Dividing Decimals Worksheets (Free, Ontario, Answer Key)
standard_text: Multiply and divide whole numbers by decimal tenths, and divide decimal numbers up to thousandths by whole numbers up to 10, using appropriate tools and strategies
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on multiplying and dividing decimals for the Ontario curriculum: × and ÷ by 10, 100 and 1000, whole numbers × tenths, decimals ÷ whole numbers, whole numbers ÷ tenths and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great for EQAO practice.
key_big: Work with whole numbers, then place the decimal point: 24 × 0.3 = 72 tenths = 7.2.
key_sub: 4.56 ÷ 4 = 456 hundredths ÷ 4 = 1.14. 12 ÷ 0.4 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes the answer smaller, and dividing by it makes the answer bigger.
body_html:
Work with whole numbers, then place the decimal point

Think of a decimal as a number of tenths, hundredths or thousandths. Do the calculation with whole numbers. Then change the answer back to a decimal. Estimate to check that the decimal point is in the right place.

× and ÷ by 10, 100 and 1000

When you multiply, every digit moves to the left. When you divide, every digit moves to the right. 1 place for 10, 2 places for 100, 3 places for 1000. The decimal point stays still.

Whole number × decimal tenths

0.3 is 3 tenths. So 4 × 0.3 is 4 groups of 3 tenths = 12 tenths = 1.2.

Example 1

24 × 0.3

0.3 is 3 tenths. 24 × 3 = 72, so 24 × 0.3 = 72 tenths = 7.2. Check: 0.3 is a bit less than half, and half of 24 is 12, so 7.2 makes sense.

Answer: 7.2

Decimal ÷ whole number

4.56 is 456 hundredths. 456 ÷ 4 = 114, so 4.56 ÷ 4 = 114 hundredths = 1.14. In long division, put the point in the answer straight above the point in the number you divide.

Example 2

4.08 ÷ 4

4 ones ÷ 4 = 1 one. 0 tenths ÷ 4 = 0 tenths. 8 hundredths ÷ 4 = 2 hundredths.

Answer: 1.02 (keep the 0 in the tenths place)

Whole number ÷ decimal tenths

2 ÷ 0.4 asks: how many jumps of 0.4 make 2? Or multiply both numbers by 10 and divide by a whole number.

Example 3

12 ÷ 0.4

Multiply both numbers by 10: 12 ÷ 0.4 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. Check: 30 × 0.4 = 12.

Answer: 30

Example 4

Apples cost $4 per kilogram. How much do 3.5 kg cost?

4 × 3.5 = 4 × 35 tenths = 140 tenths = 14. Estimate: between 4 × 3 = $12 and 4 × 4 = $16.

Answer: $14

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
24 × 0.3 = 72 (forgetting the decimal point)0.3 is 3 tenths: 72 tenths = 7.2
“Multiplying always makes bigger”× a number less than 1 makes it smaller: 36 × 0.5 = 18
“Dividing always makes smaller”÷ a number less than 1 makes it bigger: 12 ÷ 0.4 = 30
12 ÷ 0.4 = 3 (dividing by 4 instead of 0.4)Multiply both numbers by 10: 120 ÷ 4 = 30
4.56 ÷ 4 = 1.56 (dividing only the ones)Divide every digit: 4.56 ÷ 4 = 1.14
4.08 ÷ 4 = 1.2 (dropping a zero)Keep the 0 that holds the tenths place: 1.02
2.4 × 10 = 2.40 (“just add a zero”)Move every digit 1 place to the left: 24

faq.q: What does the Ontario Grade 6 math curriculum say about multiplying and dividing decimals?
faq.a: Grade 6 students multiply and divide whole numbers by decimal tenths, like 24 × 0.3 and 12 ÷ 0.4, and divide decimals up to thousandths by whole numbers up to 10, like 4.56 ÷ 4. They also multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000 and use tools and strategies to explain their thinking.

faq.q: Does multiplying always make a number bigger?
faq.a: No. Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes it smaller: 36 × 0.5 = 18. In the same way, dividing by a number less than 1 makes it bigger: 12 ÷ 0.4 = 30.

faq.q: How do you divide a whole number by a decimal, like 12 ÷ 0.4?
faq.a: Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 12 ÷ 0.4 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. Check by multiplying: 30 × 0.4 = 12.

faq.q: Is multiplying and dividing decimals on the Grade 6 EQAO math test?
faq.a: The Grade 6 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, and decimal multiplication and division are part of the Number strand. Word problems with money and measurement like the ones on this page are good practice.

items.q: The chart shows 3.7 × 10. What is the answer?
items.e: 3.7 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 3.7 × 10 = 37. 3.70 is wrong: a zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value.

items.q: The chart shows 5.2 ÷ 10. What is the answer?
items.e: 5.2 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 5.2 ÷ 10 = 0.52. 52 moves the digits the wrong way: dividing makes the number smaller.
0.64 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.64 × 100 = 64. 0.6400 only adds zeros, so it is still 0.64.
38.5 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 38.5 ÷ 100 = 0.385. 3850 moves the digits the wrong way.

items.q: Which calculation does the chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 1 place to the left, so the number was multiplied by 10. 4.15 × 10 = 41.5.

items.q: Which calculation does the chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so the number was divided by 100. 72.6 ÷ 100 = 0.726.
0.5 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005. 0.05 moves the digit only 1 place.

items.q: In 3.8 ÷ 100, how do the digits move?
items.e: 100 has 2 zeros, so every digit moves 2 places. Dividing makes the number smaller, so they move to the right: 3.8 ÷ 100 = 0.038.

2.07 × 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 2.07 × 1000 = 2070. Keep the 0 that holds the hundreds place: 2070, not 207.
83 ÷ 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 83 ÷ 1000 = 0.083. 0.83 moves the digits only 2 places.

items.q: The chart shows 0.038 × 100 = 3.8. What is the value of the red digit in the answer?
items.e: The 8 was in the thousandths place. Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so the 8 is now in the tenths place. Its value is 8 tenths = 0.8.

items.q: The chart shows 6.24 ÷ 10 = 0.624. What is the value of the red digit in the answer?
items.e: The 2 was in the tenths place. Every digit moved 1 place to the right, so the 2 is now in the hundredths place. Its value is 2 hundredths = 0.02.
14.06 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 14.06 × 10 = 140.6. 140.06 only multiplies the whole-number part. Every digit must move, including the 6.

470 ÷ 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 470 ÷ 1000 = 0.47. The last 0 is not needed after the decimal point: 0.470 = 0.47.
The 7 moves from the tenths to the tens: that is 2 places to the left, so the missing number is 100. 69.3 is 70 − 0.7, which is subtraction, not multiplication.
Use the inverse: 509 ÷ 100 = 5.09. Check: 5.09 × 100 = 509. 5.9 drops the 0 that holds the tenths place.
The 3 moves from the ones to the thousandths: 3 places to the right. So the missing number is 1000.
Use the inverse: 0.36 × 10 = 3.6. Check: 3.6 ÷ 10 = 0.36. 0.036 divides instead of multiplying.

items.q: Which calculation has the same answer as 2.5 × 100?
Which number is 1000 times as large as 0.029?
items.e: 1000 times as large means × 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. 0.029 × 1000 = 29. 0.029000 only adds zeros, so it is still 0.029.

items.q: The number line shows 4 jumps of 0.3. What is 4 × 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 is 3 tenths. 4 × 3 = 12, so 4 × 0.3 = 12 tenths = 1.2. The red dot is 2 small ticks past 1, at 1.2. 4.3 adds the numbers instead of multiplying.

items.q: The number line shows 6 jumps of 0.4. What is 6 × 0.4?
items.e: 0.4 is 4 tenths. 6 × 4 = 24, so 6 × 0.4 = 24 tenths = 2.4. The red dot is 4 small ticks past 2, at 2.4.
0.2 is 2 tenths. 6 × 2 = 12, so 6 × 0.2 = 12 tenths = 1.2. 12 forgets that 0.2 is only 2 tenths.
0.5 is 5 tenths. 7 × 5 = 35, so 7 × 0.5 = 35 tenths = 3.5. 0.35 puts the decimal point one place too far left.

items.q: 8 × 0.3 means 8 groups of 3 tenths, which is 24 tenths. What is 24 tenths as a decimal?
items.e: 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 24 tenths = 2 wholes and 4 tenths = 2.4. 0.24 is 24 hundredths.
0.3 is 3 tenths. 24 × 3 = 72, so 24 × 0.3 = 72 tenths = 7.2. 72 forgets to divide by 10. 8 is 24 ÷ 3: you multiply here, you do not divide.
0.6 is 6 tenths. 15 × 6 = 90, so 15 × 0.6 = 90 tenths = 9. 90 forgets that 0.6 is less than 1, so the answer must be less than 15.
0.7 is 7 tenths. 9 × 7 = 63, so 9 × 0.7 = 63 tenths = 6.3. You can multiply in any order: 0.7 × 9 = 9 × 0.7.
0.2 is 2 tenths. 45 × 2 = 90, so 45 × 0.2 = 90 tenths = 9. 45.2 adds 0.2 to 45 instead of multiplying.
0.4 is 4 tenths. 32 × 4 = 128, so 32 × 0.4 = 128 tenths = 12.8. 8 is 32 ÷ 4. 128 forgets to divide by 10.
0.4 is 4 ÷ 10, so the answer is 104 ÷ 10 = 10.4. 1.04 divides by 100.

items.q: Without working it out, which is true about 36 × 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 is less than 1, so 36 × 0.5 is less than 36 × 1 = 36. Multiplying by a decimal less than 1 makes the number smaller. In fact 36 × 0.5 = 18 (half of 36).

items.q: Which product is less than 50?
items.e: Only 0.9 is less than 1, so only 50 × 0.9 is less than 50 (it is 45). Multiplying by a number greater than 1 makes 50 bigger.
0.6 is 6 tenths. 230 × 6 = 1380, so 230 × 0.6 = 1380 tenths = 138. 13.8 divides by 100, but 0.6 is tenths, so divide by 10.
0.8 is 8 tenths. 125 × 8 = 1000, so 125 × 0.8 = 1000 tenths = 100. 1000 forgets that 0.8 is less than 1, so the answer must be less than 125.
0.8 is 8 tenths. 250 × 8 = 2000, so 250 × 0.8 = 2000 tenths = 200. Think: 0.8 of 250 is a bit less than 250. 2000 is far too big.
2.5 is 25 tenths. 12 × 25 = 300, so 12 × 2.5 = 300 tenths = 30. Or split it: 12 × 2 = 24 and 12 × 0.5 = 6, so 24 + 6 = 30. 24.5 forgets to multiply the 0.5 by 12.
1.5 is 15 tenths. 16 × 15 = 240, so 16 × 1.5 = 240 tenths = 24. Or split it: 16 × 1 = 16 and 16 × 0.5 = 8, so 16 + 8 = 24. 16.5 forgets to multiply the 0.5 by 16.
40 × 3 = 120, which is 10 times too big. So the missing number is 3 ÷ 10 = 0.3. Check: 40 × 0.3 = 120 tenths = 12.

items.q: Amira says 14 × 0.5 = 70. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 14 × 5 = 70, but 0.5 is 5 tenths, so 14 × 0.5 = 70 tenths = 7. Amira thought multiplying always makes a number bigger. Half of 14 is 7.
0.8 is 8 tenths. 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so 0.8 ÷ 2 = 4 tenths = 0.4. Check: 0.4 × 2 = 0.8. 1.6 multiplies instead of dividing.
2.4 is 24 tenths. 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so 2.4 ÷ 6 = 4 tenths = 0.4. Check: 0.4 × 6 = 2.4. 2.5 is 6 ÷ 2.4: it divides the wrong way round.
6.3 is 63 tenths. 63 ÷ 3 = 21, so 6.3 ÷ 3 = 21 tenths = 2.1. Check: 2.1 × 3 = 6.3. 2.3 divides only the 6 and forgets the 3 tenths.
8.4 is 84 tenths. 84 ÷ 4 = 21, so 8.4 ÷ 4 = 21 tenths = 2.1. Check: 2.1 × 4 = 8.4. 2.4 divides only the 8 and forgets the 4 tenths.
5.6 is 56 tenths. 56 ÷ 8 = 7, so 5.6 ÷ 8 = 7 tenths = 0.7. Check: 0.7 × 8 = 5.6. 5.6 is less than 8, so the answer is less than 1. 44.8 multiplies.
4.56 is 456 hundredths. 456 ÷ 4 = 114, so 4.56 ÷ 4 = 114 hundredths = 1.14. Check: 1.14 × 4 = 4.56. 1.56 divides only the 4 ones. 11.4 puts the point in the wrong place.

items.q: 4.56 is 456 hundredths. What is 456 hundredths ÷ 4?
items.e: 456 ÷ 4 = 114, and the unit stays the same: 114 hundredths = 1.14. So 4.56 ÷ 4 = 1.14.
7.25 is 725 hundredths. 725 ÷ 5 = 145, so 7.25 ÷ 5 = 145 hundredths = 1.45. Check: 1.45 × 5 = 7.25. 14.5 is 10 times too big: 7.25 ÷ 5 must be less than 2.
9.36 is 936 hundredths. 936 ÷ 3 = 312, so 9.36 ÷ 3 = 312 hundredths = 3.12. Check: 3.12 × 3 = 9.36. 3.36 divides only the 9 ones.

items.q: The quotient digits for 7.38 ÷ 3 are 2, 4, 6. Where does the decimal point go?
items.e: Put the decimal point in the quotient straight above the point in 7.38. Estimate: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so the answer is between 2 and 3. 7.38 ÷ 3 = 2.46.

items.q: The quotient digits for 5.85 ÷ 5 are 1, 1, 7. What is 5.85 ÷ 5?
items.e: The point in the quotient goes straight above the point in 5.85. Estimate: 5 ÷ 5 = 1. 5.85 ÷ 5 = 1.17. Check: 1.17 × 5 = 5.85.
12.6 is 126 tenths. 126 ÷ 7 = 18, so 12.6 ÷ 7 = 18 tenths = 1.8. Check: 1.8 × 7 = 12.6. 88.2 multiplies instead of dividing.
4.08 is 408 hundredths. 408 ÷ 4 = 102, so 4.08 ÷ 4 = 102 hundredths = 1.02. Check: 1.02 × 4 = 4.08. 1.2 drops the 0 that holds the tenths place: 4 ÷ 4 = 1 one, 0 ÷ 4 = 0 tenths, 8 ÷ 4 = 2 hundredths.
15.75 is 1575 hundredths. 1575 ÷ 7 = 225, so 15.75 ÷ 7 = 225 hundredths = 2.25. Check: 2.25 × 7 = 15.75. 22.5 puts the point in the wrong place: 14 ÷ 7 = 2, so the answer is about 2.
3.015 is 3015 thousandths. 3015 ÷ 3 = 1005, so 3.015 ÷ 3 = 1005 thousandths = 1.005. Check: 1.005 × 3 = 3.015. 1.05 and 1.5 drop the zeros that hold the tenths and hundredths places.

items.q: The quotient digits for 0.954 ÷ 9 are 0, 1, 0, 6. What is 0.954 ÷ 9?
items.e: The point goes straight above the point in 0.954. 9 tenths ÷ 9 = 1 tenth, 5 hundredths ÷ 9 = 0 hundredths (keep the 0), 54 thousandths ÷ 9 = 6 thousandths. 0.954 ÷ 9 = 0.106. 0.16 drops the 0.
2.736 is 2736 thousandths. 2736 ÷ 8 = 342, so 2.736 ÷ 8 = 342 thousandths = 0.342. Check: 0.342 × 8 = 2.736. 2.736 is less than 8, so the answer is less than 1.
1.845 is 1845 thousandths. 1845 ÷ 9 = 205, so 1.845 ÷ 9 = 205 thousandths = 0.205. Check: 0.205 × 9 = 1.845. 0.25 drops the 0 that holds the hundredths place.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 23.8 ÷ 6?
items.e: 23.8 is close to 24, and 24 ÷ 6 = 4. 143 is about 23.8 × 6: it multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Lucas says 9.45 ÷ 5 = 18.9. Use an estimate to check. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Estimate: 10 ÷ 5 = 2, so the answer is about 2, not about 19. 945 hundredths ÷ 5 = 189 hundredths, so 9.45 ÷ 5 = 1.89.

items.q: How many jumps of 0.4 make 2? Use the number line to find 2 ÷ 0.4.
items.e: Count the jumps from 0 to 2: there are 5. So 2 ÷ 0.4 = 5. Check: 5 × 0.4 = 2. 0.8 is 2 × 0.4: it multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: How many jumps of 0.2 make 1? Use the number line to find 1 ÷ 0.2.
items.e: Count the jumps from 0 to 1: there are 5. So 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5. Check: 5 × 0.2 = 1.

items.q: How many jumps of 0.5 make 3? Use the number line to find 3 ÷ 0.5.
items.e: Count the jumps from 0 to 3: there are 6 (2 in each whole). So 3 ÷ 0.5 = 6. 1.5 is 3 × 0.5: it multiplies instead of dividing.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 6 ÷ 0.3 = 60 ÷ 3 = 20. Check: 20 × 0.3 = 6. 2 is 6 ÷ 3: it forgets that 0.3 is 3 tenths, not 3.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 8 ÷ 0.2 = 80 ÷ 2 = 40. Check: 40 × 0.2 = 8. 4 is 8 ÷ 2: it forgets that 0.2 is 2 tenths.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 9 ÷ 0.1 = 90 ÷ 1 = 90. Check: 90 × 0.1 = 9. 0.9 is 9 × 0.1. There are 10 tenths in each whole, so 90 tenths in 9.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 12 ÷ 0.4 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. Check: 30 × 0.4 = 12. 4.8 is 12 × 0.4. Dividing by a number less than 1 gives a bigger answer.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 15 ÷ 0.5 = 150 ÷ 5 = 30. Check: 30 × 0.5 = 15. 7.5 is 15 × 0.5 (half of 15). How many halves are in 15? 30.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 7 ÷ 0.5 = 70 ÷ 5 = 14. Check: 14 × 0.5 = 7. 3.5 is 7 × 0.5. There are 2 halves in each whole, so 14 halves in 7.

items.q: 3 is 30 tenths and 0.6 is 6 tenths. How many groups of 6 tenths are in 30 tenths? (This is 3 ÷ 0.6.)
Without working it out, which is true about 20 ÷ 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 is less than 1, so there are more than 20 halves in 20. Dividing by a decimal less than 1 makes the answer bigger. In fact 20 ÷ 0.5 = 40. 10 is half of 20, which is 20 × 0.5.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 14 ÷ 0.7 = 140 ÷ 7 = 20. Check: 20 × 0.7 = 14. 9.8 is 14 × 0.7: it multiplies instead of dividing.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 24 ÷ 0.6 = 240 ÷ 6 = 40. Check: 40 × 0.6 = 24. 14.4 is 24 × 0.6: it multiplies instead of dividing.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 36 ÷ 0.9 = 360 ÷ 9 = 40. Check: 40 × 0.9 = 36. 4 is 36 ÷ 9: it forgets to multiply 36 by 10 as well.

items.q: Which calculation has the same answer as 12 ÷ 0.4?
items.e: Multiply both numbers by 10: 12 ÷ 0.4 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 changes only the 0.4.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 5 ÷ 0.4 = 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5. Check: 12.5 × 0.4 = 5. 2 is 5 × 0.4: it multiplies instead of dividing.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 18 ÷ 1.2 = 180 ÷ 12 = 15. Check: 15 × 1.2 = 18. 21.6 is 18 × 1.2: it multiplies instead of dividing.
Multiply both numbers by 10 so you divide by a whole number: 9 ÷ 1.5 = 90 ÷ 15 = 6. Check: 6 × 1.5 = 9. 13.5 is 9 × 1.5. Count by 1.5: 1.5, 3, 4.5, 6, 7.5, 9 is 6 jumps.
Use the inverse: 35 × 0.2 = 70 tenths = 7. Check: 7 ÷ 0.2 = 70 ÷ 2 = 35. 175 is 35 ÷ 0.2: it divides instead of multiplying.

items.q: Ethan says 16 ÷ 0.8 = 2. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 16 ÷ 0.8 = 160 ÷ 8 = 20. Ethan worked out 16 ÷ 8 and forgot to multiply 16 by 10 as well. Check: 20 × 0.8 = 16, but 2 × 0.8 is only 1.6.

items.q: Apples cost $4 per kilogram. Olivia buys 3.5 kg. How much does she pay?
items.e: 4 × 3.5 = 4 × 35 tenths = 140 tenths = $14. Check: 4 × 3 = 12 and 4 × 0.5 = 2. $7.50 adds 4 + 3.5 instead of multiplying.

items.q: A 2.25 L bottle of juice is shared equally among 5 friends. How much juice does each friend get?
items.e: 2.25 L is 225 hundredths. 225 ÷ 5 = 45, so each friend gets 45 hundredths = 0.45 L (450 mL). 11.25 L multiplies: each friend cannot get more than the whole bottle.

items.q: Priya runs 0.8 km every day for 15 days. How far does she run in all?
items.e: 15 × 0.8 = 15 × 8 tenths = 120 tenths = 12 km. 120 km forgets to divide by 10. 15.8 km adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: A sugar shack pours 12 L of maple syrup into bottles that hold 0.5 L each. How many bottles does it fill?
items.e: 12 ÷ 0.5 = 120 ÷ 5 = 24 bottles. Each litre fills 2 bottles, so 12 L fill 24. 6 bottles divides by 2 instead of 0.5.

items.q: Each batch of pancakes uses 0.3 L of milk. How much milk is needed for 14 batches?
items.e: 14 × 0.3 = 14 × 3 tenths = 42 tenths = 4.2 L. 42 L forgets to divide by 10.

items.q: Zoe cuts a 4.5 m ribbon into 9 equal pieces for the class banner. How long is each piece?
items.e: 4.5 is 45 tenths. 45 ÷ 9 = 5, so each piece is 5 tenths = 0.5 m (50 cm). 2 m is 9 ÷ 4.5: it divides the wrong way round.

items.q: One lap of the school field is 0.4 km. How many laps make 6 km for the Terry Fox Run?
items.e: 6 ÷ 0.4 = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 laps. Check: 15 × 0.4 = 6. 24 laps is 6 × 4: it forgets that 0.4 is 4 tenths.

items.q: A 3 L jug of water fills paper cups that hold 0.2 L each. How many cups can be filled?
items.e: 3 ÷ 0.2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cups. Each litre fills 5 cups. 0.6 is 3 × 0.2: it multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Canoe rental costs $18 per hour. Which is the best estimate of the cost for 2.9 hours?
items.e: 2.9 hours is close to 3 hours. $18 × 3 = $54. $36 rounds 2.9 down to 2, but 2.9 is much closer to 3.

items.q: Potatoes cost $2 per kilogram. Which is the best estimate of the cost of 4.9 kg?
items.e: 4.9 kg is about 5 kg, and 5 × $2 = $10. (The exact cost is 4.9 × 2 = $9.80.) $8 rounds 4.9 down to 4.

items.q: During a snowstorm, 2.4 cm of snow fell every hour for 8 hours. How much snow fell in all?
items.e: 8 × 2.4 = 8 × 24 tenths = 192 tenths = 19.2 cm. Check: 8 × 2 = 16 and 8 × 0.4 = 3.2. 10.4 cm adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: A 7.2 km hiking trail is split into 8 equal sections. How long is each section?
items.e: 7.2 is 72 tenths. 72 ÷ 8 = 9, so each section is 9 tenths = 0.9 km. 9 km is longer than the whole trail.

items.q: Fabric for a team banner costs $9 per metre. Owen buys 2.5 m. How much does he pay?
A pack of 6 juice boxes costs $4.86. How much is one juice box?
items.e: 486 cents ÷ 6 = 81 cents, so one box costs $0.81 (81¢). $8.10 puts the point in the wrong place. $29.16 multiplies by 6.

items.q: On a canoe trip, 9 campers share a 1.35 kg bag of trail mix equally. How much does each camper get?
items.e: 1.35 is 135 hundredths. 135 ÷ 9 = 15, so each camper gets 15 hundredths = 0.15 kg (150 g). 1.5 kg is more than the whole bag.

items.q: Leah’s dog eats 0.4 kg of food a day. How many days does a 12 kg bag last?
Four friends share a $7.92 bill for snacks at the skating rink. About how much does each friend pay?
items.e: $7.92 is close to $8, and $8 ÷ 4 = $2 each. (Exactly: 792¢ ÷ 4 = 198¢ = $1.98.) $32 multiplies by 4 instead of dividing.

items.q: Kai works out the cost of 3.5 kg of grapes at $6 per kilogram and gets $210. What is the correct cost?
items.e: 6 × 35 = 210, but 3.5 is 35 tenths, so 6 × 3.5 = 210 tenths = $21. Estimate: 6 × 3 = 18 and 6 × 4 = 24, so the cost is between $18 and $24.

items.q: Maya buys 3.5 kg of apples at $4 per kilogram. She pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: Cost: 4 × 3.5 = $14. Change: $20 − $14 = $6. $14 is the cost, not the change. $12.50 adds 4 + 3.5 instead of multiplying.

items.q: Noah makes 3 L of lemonade for a stand. He pours it into cups that hold 0.2 L each and sells every cup for 50¢. How much money does he collect?
